{"rule":"Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and, in the text field, an original fictional passage of about 250 words that comes immediately AFTER the current text in the same invented story.","text":"The brass shuddered beneath her palm. A thin seam of blue light appeared around the drawer, brightening with every beat of the watch.

“Now what?” Mara asked.

The stranger’s gaze lifted to the glass ceiling. “Now you listen.”

At first there was only the river’s heavy rush. Then came a small, familiar sound: her mother humming, off-key, the tune she had sung while pitching the tent. Mara pressed the ribbon to her cheek. The melody rose from the drawer, accompanied by rain on canvas and the crackle of a fire.

A second sound followed: her mother’s breath, ragged and shallow. Hospital lights flashed behind Mara’s eyes. She remembered a narrow bed, a paper cup of water, her own fingers wrapped around her mother’s.

The watch ticked faster.

Mara gripped the drawer handle. “I’m not leaving any of it behind.”

The stranger said nothing. The silver in her eyes had gone almost dark.

The drawer slid open by itself.

A voice spilled out, soft as the first drops of rain. “Mara, sweetheart. You don’t have to be brave for me.”

Mara’s knees buckled. She had remembered the words, but not the warmth in them, nor the faint smile tucked into the last syllable. The voice faded, and the drawer began to close.

“No.” She caught its edge.

The river struck the glass overhead. A crack raced across the ceiling, and moonlight poured into the room.

The stranger reached for her. “If you hold on, it will take something else.”

Mara looked at the ribbon, then at the watch. Its hands spun wildly.

“Then let it take the fear,” she said.

The drawer clicked open once more."}
